options.text: The Paramecium is a complete living organism even though it is one cell; the muscle cell from the human body chart is not itself a complete organism.
The Paramecium is an incomplete living organism because it has only one cell.
The muscle cell from the human body chart is itself a complete organism.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem:
Vivaan watches a Paramecium under the school microscope. It swims, takes in food, and divides on its own. A classmate says it cannot be a complete living organism because it has only one cell. Vivaan also studies one muscle cell on a chart of the human body, and recalls that some microorganisms such as bacteria are unicellular.

Answer both parts.

part_answers.answer: A unicellular microorganism such as Paramecium carries out all survival functions in one cell, so it is a complete organism; a muscle cell is only one part of a multicellular body.

teacher.key_rationale: Unicellular microbes can be complete organisms; a single cell taken from a multicellular body is not, and not every microorganism is unicellular.
